Editor's Note: The following contains spoilers for Tracker Season 4, Episode 2.After a solid Season 4 premiere, Tracker has returned in full form with Colter Shaw (Justin Hartley) ready for his next adventures. The CBS drama continues to lean into its change of production location by highlighting the new scenery of Sunny California. "Switchback" takes our hero up the Pacific Coast for an adventure in hiking that gets a bit twisted along the way, but it's nothing that he can't handle. As Tracker turns Colter on to his next new case, the series sets up some subplots that will likely string across the next several episodes. So, strap in, because here's where Colter ran off to this week.

blocks.c: Colter in Tracker

blocks.x: This week's Tracker begins with mother-daughter duo Leanne (Sarah Jane Morris) and Kayla Reilly (Mallory Bechtel) going missing on the Pacific Divide Trail after being stalked by someone taking photos of them from afar. Distracted by the fact that his brother Russell (Jensen Ackles) hasn't gotten back to him, Colter leaves his brother a message. Considering this is the first season where Russell hasn't appeared in one of the first two episodes since Season 1, Tracker appears to be keeping us on edge here regarding that deal Colter's brother made last season. But Colter doesn't wallow for long, because he soon gets the details from Randy (Chris Lee) about the latest case, who turns him onto the $15,000 reward posted by Leanne's other daughter Anya (Skyler Day). They've only been missing for a day, but everything's a bit strange — as these jobs typically are. Colter heads to the trailhead to speak with Anya, who reveals that they were all in the area to honor their deceased father by spreading their ashes; only she didn't go with her mother and sister because of her own family. So, partnering with "trail angel" Becca (Erica Hernandez), Colter heads off in search of the missing pair.

Back in Denver, Reenie (Fiona Rene) returns to the rest of the cast's temporary office at Maxine's (Kathleen Robertson) firm. This is sort of a strange way to shoehorn Maxine back into the story after it felt like her part in the show was done last year, but what can you do? She doesn't appear here, however, and instead, Reenie finds herself having a heart-to-heart with Mel (Cassady McClincy Zhang), who asks for help finding out what really happened to her mom. Recently, she found out that a man named Eric Jefferies, a former military officer seemingly "honorably discharged," worked with her mother in the weeks before her murder. Reenie plans to poke around, using her own military contacts to dig something up. Sometimes we forget that Reenie was an "Air Force brat," but it's moments like these where that little bit of Tracker trivia comes in handy.

blocks.c: Jensen Ackles as Russell Shaw and Justin Hartley as Colter Shaw in Tracker season 3, episode 1

blocks.x: Meanwhile, back in California, Colter and Becca make quick work of the trail. It isn't long before they discern the area where the women probably went off-trail, and they eventually come across a makeshift campsite seemingly put together by a man named Jonah Gammon (Billy Lush). Boasting a bounty of stolen material from various hikers and campers, Jonah's campsite is like a rat's nest, but it's the perfect place for their next clue. Finding some of the Reillys' things, Colter and Becca run into Leanne, who has a serious gash on her head. She claims that Kayla — who was injured after the pair ran from their stalker — was taken by whoever attacked her in the first place. The first assumption here is that Jonah is the culprit.

blocks.x: It isn't long before Colter tracks down Jonah and forces him to talk. The only problem is, he wasn't the one who attacked the women. Still, Colter gets the vagabond to spill, and he explains that he saw Kayla being taken by a man in a baseball hat down some fire road access path. Since he was trying not to be seen, he didn't get a good look, but he described the man's truck as being both old and brown — which could probably describe nearly any run-down pickup in the area. Fortunately, Jonah says he may have seen it up by Sierra Junction. Before Colter leaves him, he tells Jonah to go get some help, because living up here all on his lonesome will ultimately get him killed. It's a small moment, but a sober reminder that Colter genuinely cares for those around him, and rather than just call the police to come and pick him up, he would rather turn Jonah on to the kind of help he needs to get back on his feet.

blocks.c: Abby McEnany as Velma Bruin in Tracker

blocks.x: Calling Randy, Colter discovers that Kayla and Leanne had been at Rise & Shine, a local watering hole, a few days earlier. "This wasn't some random snatch and grab," Colter concludes. Having gotten Leanne the help she needs, Colter and Becca head to Rise & Shine and split up to search for clues. This leads Colter to speak to Diana Sanders (Amy Farrington), a local who was working the day that the Reillys stopped in. Unfortunately, she claims to have seen nothing since she was working the pick-up window. Still, she takes a photo of Kayla to see if any of the locals know anything more. But what may have been a dead end quickly turns into just the break in the case they needed, as Becca is nearly killed in a hit-and-run by the mysterious brown truck Jonah saw.

blocks.c: Jensen Ackles as Russell Shaw in Tracker

blocks.x: Russell Shaw may be returning soon, but Ackles is staying booked and busy.

blocks.c: Fiona Rene as Reenie Greene and Eric Graise as Bobby Exley in Tracker

blocks.x: After stabilizing her, Colter chases after the vehicle only to find it abandoned on a trail. He chases the driver into a barn, takes a shot at him, and attempts to coax him out to find Kayla. Unfortunately, he refuses to let Colter treat his wound, instead "taking his own way out," as our hero says. In doing so, he takes Kayla's location with him. Investigating the truck itself, he finds blood on the bed and confirms that she had been stashed there after all. Discovering that the driver's name was Jack Owens (Brandon Knabe), he calls Randy to find out everything he can about the kidnapper — which, given how the episode began by reminding us that cell service is really spotty here, feels like a bit of a cheat. Anyway, as it turns out, Jack works at Rise & Shine and lives somewhere nearby. However, when Colter goes to investigate the house, he finds nobody there. Nevertheless, the poor girl is nearby, trapped in another building on the property...

blocks.x: As it turns out, Diana, the woman Colter met at Rise & Shine, was Jack's mother, and knew all about his "urges." She tells Kayla that it's her job to clean up her son's mess. According to Randy, Diana was in a psyche ward a few decades ago and was let out on a probationary period to have Jack. Either way, she's not alright upstairs, and it's because of that mental imbalance that she has thus enabled her son to lean into the same ideas that got her in trouble in the first place. Colter quickly discovers that Kayla is being kept nearby on the same property and arrives just in time to keep Diana from pulling a bullet in the young woman after she so valiantly escaped. Although Diana was prepared for an old-fashioned Mexican stand-off, Kayla knocks her out, and Colter reunites her with the rest of her family.

Back in Denver, Reenie's military contact pulls through and gets the information Mel requested about Eric Jefferies. Apparently, his discharge was far less than "honorable," leading her to become more suspicious about the circumstances surrounding Mel's mother's murder. But rather than inform Mel of what she's found — or even Colter, at this point, who is kind of the guy you want in the loop on a case like this — she lets it be for now. And, frankly, we're not really sure why. Wouldn't Mel rather know the truth? She didn't know this Jefferies guy personally, so why would learning about a dishonorable discharge affect her negatively? Either way, Tracker doesn't spend enough time on it to offer any real answers.

blocks.c: image-3.png

blocks.x: Instead, "Switchback" ends with a heartwarming departure from the Reilly family, who are anxious to move on from the Pacific Divide Trail and spread their husband/father's ashes elsewhere. On top of that, we get an almost romantic send-off for Becca, who is definitely the sort of love interest we could see Colter trying to make things work with. On his way out, Russell finally texts his brother with an apology and a promise that they'll talk soon. Thanks for teasing us with more Jensen Ackles, Tracker, we can't wait!

Editor's Note: The following contains spoilers for Tracker Season 4, Episode 2.After a solid Season 4 premiere, Tracker has returned in full form with Colter Shaw (Justin Hartley) ready for his next adventures. As Tracker turns Colter on to his next new case, the series sets up some subplots that will likely string across the next several episodes. So, strap in, because here's where Colter ran off to this week.

"Switchback" Keeps Colter Shaw in Sunny California

This week's Tracker begins with mother-daughter duo Leanne (Sarah Jane Morris) and Kayla Reilly (Mallory Bechtel) going missing on the Pacific Divide Trail after being stalked by someone taking photos of them from afar. Distracted by the fact that his brother Russell (Jensen Ackles) hasn't gotten back to him, Colter leaves his brother a message. Considering this is the first season where Russell hasn't appeared in one of the first two episodes since Season 1, Tracker appears to be keeping us on edge here regarding that deal Colter's brother made last season. But Colter doesn't wallow for long, because he soon gets the details from Randy (Chris Lee) about the latest case, who turns him onto the $15,000 reward posted by Leanne's other daughter Anya (Skyler Day). They've only been missing for a day, but everything's a bit strange — as these jobs typically are. Colter heads to the trailhead to speak with Anya, who reveals that they were all in the area to honor their deceased father by spreading their ashes; only she didn't go with her mother and sister because of her own family. So, partnering with "trail angel" Becca (Erica Hernandez), Colter heads off in search of the missing pair.

Back in Denver, Reenie (Fiona Rene) returns to the rest of the cast's temporary office at Maxine's (Kathleen Robertson) firm. This is sort of a strange way to shoehorn Maxine back into the story after it felt like her part in the show was done last year, but what can you do? She doesn't appear here, however, and instead, Reenie finds herself having a heart-to-heart with Mel (Cassady McClincy Zhang), who asks for help finding out what really happened to her mom. Recently, she found out that a man named Eric Jefferies, a former military officer seemingly "honorably discharged," worked with her mother in the weeks before her murder. Reenie plans to poke around, using her own military contacts to dig something up. Sometimes we forget that Reenie was an "Air Force brat," but it's moments like these where that little bit of Tracker trivia comes in handy.

Meanwhile, back in California, Colter and Becca make quick work of the trail. It isn't long before they discern the area where the women probably went off-trail, and they eventually come across a makeshift campsite seemingly put together by a man named Jonah Gammon (Billy Lush). Boasting a bounty of stolen material from various hikers and campers, Jonah's campsite is like a rat's nest, but it's the perfect place for their next clue. Finding some of the Reillys' things, Colter and Becca run into Leanne, who has a serious gash on her head. She claims that Kayla — who was injured after the pair ran from their stalker — was taken by whoever attacked her in the first place. The first assumption here is that Jonah is the culprit.

Image via CBS

It isn't long before Colter tracks down Jonah and forces him to talk. The only problem is, he wasn't the one who attacked the women. Still, Colter gets the vagabond to spill, and he explains that he saw Kayla being taken by a man in a baseball hat down some fire road access path. Since he was trying not to be seen, he didn't get a good look, but he described the man's truck as being both old and brown — which could probably describe nearly any run-down pickup in the area. Fortunately, Jonah says he may have seen it up by Sierra Junction. Before Colter leaves him, he tells Jonah to go get some help, because living up here all on his lonesome will ultimately get him killed. It's a small moment, but a sober reminder that Colter genuinely cares for those around him, and rather than just call the police to come and pick him up, he would rather turn Jonah on to the kind of help he needs to get back on his feet.

Calling Randy, Colter discovers that Kayla and Leanne had been at Rise & Shine, a local watering hole, a few days earlier. "This wasn't some random snatch and grab," Colter concludes. Having gotten Leanne the help she needs, Colter and Becca head to Rise & Shine and split up to search for clues. This leads Colter to speak to Diana Sanders (Amy Farrington), a local who was working the day that the Reillys stopped in. Unfortunately, she claims to have seen nothing since she was working the pick-up window. Still, she takes a photo of Kayla to see if any of the locals know anything more. But what may have been a dead end quickly turns into just the break in the case they needed, as Becca is nearly killed in a hit-and-run by the mysterious brown truck Jonah saw.

Russell Shaw may be returning soon, but Ackles is staying booked and busy.

After stabilizing her, Colter chases after the vehicle only to find it abandoned on a trail. He chases the driver into a barn, takes a shot at him, and attempts to coax him out to find Kayla. Unfortunately, he refuses to let Colter treat his wound, instead "taking his own way out," as our hero says. In doing so, he takes Kayla's location with him. Investigating the truck itself, he finds blood on the bed and confirms that she had been stashed there after all. Discovering that the driver's name was Jack Owens (Brandon Knabe), he calls Randy to find out everything he can about the kidnapper — which, given how the episode began by reminding us that cell service is really spotty here, feels like a bit of a cheat. Anyway, as it turns out, Jack works at Rise & Shine and lives somewhere nearby. However, when Colter goes to investigate the house, he finds nobody there. Nevertheless, the poor girl is nearby, trapped in another building on the property...

"Switchback" Concludes With a Standoff and a Revelation

Image via CBS

As it turns out, Diana, the woman Colter met at Rise & Shine, was Jack's mother, and knew all about his "urges." She tells Kayla that it's her job to clean up her son's mess. According to Randy, Diana was in a psyche ward a few decades ago and was let out on a probationary period to have Jack. Either way, she's not alright upstairs, and it's because of that mental imbalance that she has thus enabled her son to lean into the same ideas that got her in trouble in the first place. Colter quickly discovers that Kayla is being kept nearby on the same property and arrives just in time to keep Diana from pulling a bullet in the young woman after she so valiantly escaped. Although Diana was prepared for an old-fashioned Mexican stand-off, Kayla knocks her out, and Colter reunites her with the rest of her family.

Back in Denver, Reenie's military contact pulls through and gets the information Mel requested about Eric Jefferies. Apparently, his discharge was far less than "honorable," leading her to become more suspicious about the circumstances surrounding Mel's mother's murder. But rather than inform Mel of what she's found — or even Colter, at this point, who is kind of the guy you want in the loop on a case like this — she lets it be for now. And, frankly, we're not really sure why. Wouldn't Mel rather know the truth? She didn't know this Jefferies guy personally, so why would learning about a dishonorable discharge affect her negatively? Either way, Tracker doesn't spend enough time on it to offer any real answers.

Instead, "Switchback" ends with a heartwarming departure from the Reilly family, who are anxious to move on from the Pacific Divide Trail and spread their husband/father's ashes elsewhere. On top of that, we get an almost romantic send-off for Becca, who is definitely the sort of love interest we could see Colter trying to make things work with. On his way out, Russell finally texts his brother with an apology and a promise that they'll talk soon. Thanks for teasing us with more Jensen Ackles, Tracker, we can't wait!
